{{Short description|Definition by exhaustively listing all of the objects a term applies to}}
{{One source|date=November 2025}}

An '''enumerative definition'''<ref>{{cite web |title=Enumerative-definition Definition & Meaning {{!}} YourDictionary |url=https://www.yourdictionary.com/enumerative-definition |website=yourdictionary.com |publisher=LoveToKnow Media |access-date=5 November 2025}}</ref> of a concept or term is a special type of [[extensional definition]] that gives an explicit and exhaustive listing of all the [[object (philosophy)|object]]s that fall under the concept or term in question.  Enumerative definitions are only possible for finite sets and only practical for relatively small sets.

==Example==
An example of an enumerative definition for the set<br><br>
'''[[extant species|extant]] [[monotreme]] species'''<br><br>
(for which the [[intensional definition]] is "species of currently-living mammals that [[oviparity|lay eggs]]") would be:
: [[platypus|platypuses]]
: echidnae:
:: [[short-beaked echidna]]
:: long-beaked echidnae:
::: [[Sir David's long-beaked echidna]]
::: [[eastern long-beaked echidna]]
::: [[western long-beaked echidna]]
